statement: Trimming the vent moves the closed note at least 50 cents each way: plugging it lowers the note, reaming it to 3.5 mm raises it
rationale: A first print of a mouth-blown vessel flute is expected within about +-10 % of the model, 165 cents (input vessel-flute-acoustics-notes, sections 0 and 3). The recordings tolerate +-8 %, 133 cents (input coo-pitch-analysis). The trim has to cover the difference, about 32 cents, with margin; 50 cents each way is the lead's number. A worst-case first print, 15 to 20 % off, is NOT covered by the vent and means a reprint with a corrected window. The upward figure is the closed form's and is low: the solve gives about 11 cents more.

mechanism.how: The closed note with the vent plugged, as printed, and reamed to the largest diameter that was solved, by the same closed form as C1; the smaller of the two shifts is held to the limit.
